claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 4 years old. I live here in the UK with Alex, and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have Alex who is 4 years old, and you live in the UK with him.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or pay for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm the one who takes care of him - I pay for his food, clothes, school things, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Just a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now, to complete the assessment:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and have the right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex was in care for a little while - about a month or so. But that's finished now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. To clarify this important detail:

**Is Alex now back living with you full-time, and if so, when exactly did he return home from care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is back living with me full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One more question about the care situation:

**How long ago did Alex return home from care? And while he was in care for that month, did he spend any regular time at home with you (for example, weekends or specific days each week)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been back home with me now, and while he was in care for those 4 weeks, he stayed there full-time - he didn't come home for weekends or anything during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. One final question:

**How long has Alex been back home with you since returning from care? Has it been more than a few weeks/months, or did he only recently return?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been back home with me now - it's been recent enough that I'm just sorting things out and that's why I'm checking about the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements for Child Benefit:

✓ Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
✓ You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
✓ You're responsible for Alex - he lives with you and you pay for all his needs
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ Alex is now back home with you full-time

Regarding the period when Alex was in care: Since he was only there for approximately 4 weeks (about a month), this is below the 8-week threshold that would affect Child Benefit entitlement. According to the rules, Child Benefit is only affected if a child is in care for more than 8 weeks.

**Next steps:**
If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can make a claim now. If you were previously claiming and stopped during Alex's time in care, you should be able to resume your claim.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.
